headlines.title: 사과 29%↓·돼지고기 13%↓ 생산자물가 3개월만에 하락
headlines.summary: 10월 생산자물가 전월比 0.1% 하락 농림수산품 변동률 빼면 0.2% 상승 11월 유가 15% 하락…도시가스 올라 10월 생산자물가가 석 달 만에 떨어졌다. 추석 명절 수요가 사라지고 사과 작황이 좋아지면서 농축산물 가격이 큰 폭으로 내린 영향이다. 국제유가 상승 여파에 공산품은 오름세를 이어갔다.

headlines.title: 올해 고랭지감자 생산량 36.6% 급증 … 고추·참깨도 증가
headlines.summary: 핵심요약 국가데이터처, 2026년 생산량 조사 결과 재배면적 확대와 기상여건 개선 영향 국가데이터처 제공 올해 고추와 참깨, 고랭지감자 생산량이 모두 전년보다 증가한 것으로 나타났다. 특히 고랭지감자는 재배면적 확대와 기상여건 개선에 힘입어 생산량이 36.6% 늘었다.

key_headlines.title: South Korea Achieves Historic $1 Trillion Annual Export Milestone
key_headlines.summary: South Korea reached a record $1.076 trillion in annual exports, with semiconductors and cosmetics leading growth. Small and medium-sized enterprises also surpassed $100 billion in exports for the first time.

key_headlines.title: HBM Semiconductor Chips Become South Korea's Export Star After 13 Years
key_headlines.summary: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) chips, once dismissed as having no market, have emerged as a major driver of South Korea's semiconductor exports, which account for 43% of total exports. SK Hynix continues investing heavily in HBM development.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Crashes to 4,900 Level with Lowest Trading Volume in 12 Years
key_headlines.summary: South Korean stock market experienced sharp declines with KOSPI and KOSDAQ both falling over 5% on so-called 'Black Friday,' reaching the lowest daily trading volume in 12 years at 240 million shares.

key_headlines.title: US Approves Semiconductor Exports to China Despite Restrictions
key_headlines.summary: The United States approved exports of approximately 880,000 semiconductor chips from Nvidia and AMD to Chinese companies including Tencent and Alibaba, despite restrictions aimed at China's military.

key_headlines.title: South Korea's Trade Deficit with China Widens Excluding Semiconductors
key_headlines.summary: Excluding semiconductors, South Korea's trade with China shows a $41.5 billion deficit, as Chinese electric vehicle imports surge and Korean automobile exports decline due to rising domestic production costs.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea achieved a historic milestone by reaching $1.076 trillion in annual exports, with semiconductors and cosmetics leading the surge. High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) chips, once considered a failed product with no market demand, have remarkably re-emerged as a major export driver after 13 years. Small and medium enterprises also broke through the $100 billion export barrier for the first time. Additionally, the automotive sector contributed significantly to export growth, increasing 5.4 times over the past 25 years. These achievements underscore South Korea's strength in advanced technology and manufacturing sectors.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea will hold its final monetary policy decision of the year next week (November 26), with markets anticipating a potential interest rate adjustment. The US Federal Reserve's December FOMC meeting is scheduled for December 8-9, with market expectations of rate increases based on recent economic data. South Korea's October producer price index declined 0.1% month-on-month for the first time in three months, primarily due to falling agricultural and livestock prices following the Chuseok holiday season. Despite the decline, excluding agricultural products, industrial producer prices rose 0.2%, while international oil price fluctuations affected the overall outlook.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korea's stock market experienced a severe 'Black Friday' on November 20, with both KOSPI and KOSDAQ falling over 5% amid weak investor sentiment and foreign capital outflows totaling over 2 trillion won. KOSPI breached the 4,900 level, reaching 10-month lows, while daily trading volume hit the lowest level in 12 years at approximately 240 million shares. The disappointing performance of Anthropic's IPO failed to revive interest in AI-related stocks, with risk-aversion sentiment dominating the market. Government bond yields across all maturities declined as investors shifted toward safer assets amid heightened market volatility.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's semiconductor sector remains a critical export driver, accounting for 43% of total exports and reaching $400 billion in the first 10 months of the year. HBM semiconductors developed by SK Hynix have transformed from a struggling technology into a major export success story. However, excluding semiconductor exports, South Korea faces a $41.5 billion trade deficit with China, as Chinese electric vehicles gain market share while Korean automobile exports decline. Rising domestic production costs for secondary batteries force some Korean companies to import products manufactured in Chinese factories, further widening the non-semiconductor trade gap with China.
sections.Real Estate: South Korea's housing market shows mixed signals with 6,295 housing units available for public subscription in the week of November 24, representing a 3.7-fold increase compared to the previous week. The government announced that the 2027 housing public announcement rate will remain unchanged at 69.0%, maintaining stable property tax burdens despite variations in regional real estate values. Major redevelopment projects continue, including the Jamsil Jeonju Apartment reconstruction, which offers potential capital gains of up to 2.4 billion won for successful bidders. Property acquisition regulations in Seoul and controlled zones cap loan-to-value ratios at 40%, limiting purchasing power in major metropolitan areas.
sections.International Economy: South Korea's trade surplus with the United States exceeded $100 billion for the first time, raising concerns about potential additional US tariffs under the Trump administration, particularly targeting automobiles and components. The Trump administration has signaled willingness to implement up to 25% tariffs on imported vehicles and threatened tax penalties on US companies establishing data centers abroad. The UK and EU are negotiating to lower economic barriers and facilitate youth employment, though disputes remain over Chinese electric vehicle tariffs and other key issues. The Fed is considering maintaining flexibility on interest rate decisions, with recent comments from Fed officials indicating all options remain on the table for the December FOMC meeting.
sections.AI & Economy: Anthropic's initial public offering on NASDAQ, which was intended to revitalize AI sector momentum, failed to sustain investor interest as the stock declined 8.5% by its second trading day. Concerns over AI infrastructure investment costs, profitability challenges, and funding availability, combined with uncertainties around US monetary policy, have dampened enthusiasm for AI-related stocks. The Employment and Labor Minister conducted surprise inspections of national credential examination sites following an AI cheating scandal involving a tax accountant exam top scorer. The departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may reshape AI industry investment dynamics, potentially reducing financial support for AI startups dependent on Nvidia funding while creating opportunities for competitors like Google with proprietary semiconductors.
sections.Others: HS Hwasung received the highest safety management rating (SA1) for construction, demonstrating excellence in industrial accident prevention and workplace safety. The UK is pushing to lower economic barriers with the EU while maintaining disagreements over tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles. The US Senate rejected a resolution to end military involvement in Iran for the second time, as Republican lawmakers largely opposed the measure despite Democratic support. Analyst insights suggest that Nvidia's weakened financing support for AI startups, particularly cloud chip rental companies like NeoCloud, may face significant challenges in securing future capital.
